messages:
Anya: Heads up — getting sporadic 503s on presigned upload requests. Looks like path normalization collapsed double-slashes and our rewrite rule stripped Host, which breaks S3 sig validation. Repro below, can @Sam take a look?
Sam: On it. Can you paste a minimal request + gateway rewrite config you saw?
Anya: Sure — request log snippet:
```
POST /v1/uploads//private/abc?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Signature=... HTTP/1.1
Host: files.redwood.dev
User-Agent: curl/7.x
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----
```
Gateway applied config (summary):
- path_normalize: collapse_slashes
- strip_headers: [Host, X-Debug]
- inject_headers: [X-Forwarded-For]
We see rewrite applied before auth check, so S3 signature mismatches.
Mike: Stripping Host is usually safe for internal routable services, but presigned S3 URLs rely on exact host + canonicalized path. We should special-case endpoints that contain S3 signature query params.
Sam: Agreed. Two options: (1) preserve Host when query contains X-Amz-Signature or X-Amz-Algorithm, or (2) preserve Host only for routes that match /v1/uploads and have query with X-Amz-.* token. Which do we prefer?
Julia: If we special-case by header/query, remember cache keys & quota: preserving Host changes cache key semantics (Host can vary by tenant). We need to ensure this won't blow up our shard/caching assumptions. Maybe preserve but exclude from cache key unless explicitly enabled. Also the console rollout UX should present a dry-run toggle.
Sam: Draft rule suggestion (for runtime config):
```yaml
- name: preserve-s3-host-for-presigned-uploads
  match:
    path_prefix: /v1/uploads
    query_contains: ["X-Amz-Signature", "X-Amz-Algorithm"]
  actions:
    - preserve_header: Host
    - normalize_path: collapse_slashes
    - telemetry: emit_event: rewrite.decision
      tags: [preserve_host, presigned_upload]
  rollout:
    mode: gradual
    dry_run: true
```
Mike: Nice. Make sure the telemetry tag includes original_path and final_path so we can assert normalization didn't break the signature (in dry-run). Also tag tenant_id if present.
Anya: Telemetry event idea: rewrite.decision with fields: rule_id, match_reason, original_host, preserved_host, original_path, normalized_path, trace_id. We can use that to create an alert if signature failures spike after rollout.
Julia: One more gotcha — some clients depend on trailing slash semantics. collapse_slashes -> "/a//b" => "/a/b" is fine, but "/a//" -> "/a/" can change canonicalization. Add test vectors to the eval harness.
Sam: I'll open a tiny RFC PR with config patch + test cases. Plan: dry-run rollout for 48h, collect rewrite.decision metrics, then flip preserve_host on in enforced mode if no regressions.
platform-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy triggered for rewrite-engine v2 at 2142004500 — rollout mode: gradual (10% -> 50%) — logs: https://ci.redwood.dev/rewrites/2142004500
Anya: Thanks. @Mike @Julia please add any extra test cases to the PR. I'll follow up with per-tenant telemetry dashboard widgets (rewrite decisions, per-route signature failures). :thumbsup:
Mike: Adding tests now.
Julia: Will update console rollout UI notes to include a "telemetry preview" panel.
Sam: PR: https://git.redwood.dev/platform/rewrite-rules/pulls/78 — includes dry-run and telemetry schema.
Anya: Marking as blocking for next canary bump until we validate metrics.
Sam: Acknowledged.
